Why combine them. Neither database alone is complete, and the gaps are mostly metadata rather than coverage: papers are usually present in the other database but arrive without a usable acknowledgment. Scopus keeps a single funder per paper, so a centre can be dropped from a record it otherwise holds; WoS carries acknowledgment text for only about a third of its records, but keeps it in full when it does. Those two failures are independent, so the union recovers work neither would report alone. It remains a lower bound — a paper whose acknowledgment is missing from both is invisible to both. For records shared across databases, the Scopus document type is retained; a record Scopus classifies as a review or conference paper does not re-enter the journal-article total merely because WoS labels it Article. That is why the retained WoS component can be slightly smaller than the WoS-only dashboard.

The gaps are not confined to marginal work. Of the ten most-cited articles here, 6 were found only by Web of Science and 3 only by Scopus — each invisible to a study using the other database alone. The single most-cited article in this corpus — Stable, Single-Layer MX2 Transition-Metal Oxides and Dichalcogenides in a Honey (2012, 1,341 citations) — was found only by Web of Science, so a Scopus-only study would not report it at all.

Journal quality

Share of ranked articles by SCImago SJR quartile, matched to each paper's publication year. The number above each bar is that year's ranked article count.
SCImago for every paper, including the WoS ones. WoS ships its own JCR-style categories, but mixing two quartile systems in one column would make the distribution meaningless — a "Q1" would mean different things in different rows. Scopus records join SJR on source-id first, WoS-only records on ISSN; the two systems agree on 99% of the papers both databases hold. 28 of 2,768 articles are in journals SJR does not rank.

Citations per year

For papers both databases hold, the higher of the two counts — each index sees only its own citing papers, so neither is definitive and the larger is the better lower bound. Counts are never summed.

Turkish institutions

By number of articles acknowledging TRUBA, across both databases. 395 institutions in total.
Scopus names Turkish institutions in Turkish ("Cumhuriyet Üniversitesi"), WoS in English ("Cumhuriyet University"), so the two are merged by a normalisation that folds Turkish characters, translates institutional words and compares tokens without regard to order. It matches the large institutions reliably; the long tail of single-paper affiliations may still hold near-duplicates.

Method. Union of the Scopus and Web of Science acknowledgment corpora, journal articles only. Merged on DOI (lowercased); 25 records carry no DOI and were merged on a normalised title instead. Publication year taken from Scopus where present, else WoS — the two disagree on 28 papers. Citations are the higher of the two counts, never the sum. A paper counts as open access if either database says so. Quartiles are SCImago SJR throughout, matched to each paper's publication year.

Institution and researcher rankings are deliberately absent: only the WoS side carries organisation and author identifiers here, so a union-wide ranking would describe the WoS subset while appearing to cover everything. Those views live on the per-database dashboards.
